item.title: Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa plans to protect citizens from data centres, warns Musk to submit to 'their terms'
item.description: Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has highlighted her plans to bring in “laws to protect Texans” from data centres, which she said were taking advantage of rural communities in the state.
item.content:encoded:
Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa plans to protect citizens from data centres, warns Musk to submit to 'their terms' Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has highlighted her plans to bring in “laws to protect Texans” from data centres, which she said were taking advantage of rural communities in the state. ANI | Updated: 06-11-2026 09:53 IST | Created: 06-11-2026 09:53 IST

Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa (L) and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk (R) (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has highlighted her plans to bring in “laws to protect Texans” from data centres, which she said were taking advantage of rural communities in the state. Speaking to CNN, Hinojosa stated, “Right now, what has happened is data centres have moved into mostly rural communities, and there are no rules and laws to protect Texans, and Texans are being taken advantage of.” She maintained that Texas has been a pro-business state; however, she aims at business partnerships that benefit Texans. "We have always been a pro-business state in Texas, but what changes now with me as governor is it has to be a partnership that benefits Texans,” she told CNN. "So the difference is we will have laws to protect Texans, and we need to stop what we’re doing with data centres until we have those protections. We can have a strong economy, strong industry and protections for the people of Texas. Those things are not mutually exclusive, and I’ll make sure, as governor, I lead to ensure that happens," she added. While she did not rule out building of data centres in Texas, she discussed the communities having a stake in decision-making. She said, "It is not that I hate data centres. I hate the way they are taking advantage of Texas. And that stops when I’m governor.” When asked whether SpaceX CEO Elon Musk might move out of Texas, Gina Hinojosa said, "We can have a strong working relationship with Musk and his companies, but it has to be on our terms. It cannot be just running over the people of Texas." When asked about blocking the sale of a Texas state park to SpaceX, and whether Musk might leave the state over itm the Governor-elect said, “We have to have balance. These are our beaches we’re talking about. I mean, selling our beach to Elon Musk is just something that is almost unimaginable. It’s unacceptable. Our beaches are enshrined in our Texas Constitution as being free and open to the people of Texas because they are our beaches." Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor's race, defeating Republican Governor Greg Abbott. Hinojosa ended more than three decades of Republican domination in the office as the first Democrat elected governor of Texas since Ann Richards in 1990 and the state's first Latina governor. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Australia ropes in Michael Hussey as coaching consultant for 2027 Ashes, ODI World Cup, 2028 Olympics Australia have appointed former batter Michael Hussey as a coaching consultant for the 2027 Ashes and ODI World Cup, while also assigning him the role of T20 advisor for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and the T20 World Cup, which will be jointly hosted by Australia and New Zealand ANI | Updated: 06-11-2026 09:52 IST | Created: 06-11-2026 09:52 IST

Michael Hussey. (Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Australia have appointed former batter Michael Hussey as a coaching consultant for the 2027 Ashes and ODI World Cup, while also assigning him the role of T20 advisor for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and the T20 World Cup, which will be jointly hosted by Australia and New Zealand. Hussey has undertaken short-term assignments with the Australian team under head coach Andrew McDonald in recent years, primarily serving as an additional batting consultant ahead of the annual Perth Test, as per Cricinfo. However, his involvement has been limited by his commentary commitments and coaching roles with Chennai Super Kings in the IPL and Welsh Fire in The Hundred. Hussey was also approached to join long-time colleague Stephen Fleming's coaching setup after the New Zealander took charge of England's Test team earlier this year. However, he turned down the opportunity in favour of a more substantial consultancy role with Australia. His new assignment will begin with Australia's upcoming T20I series against England, before he assists the team in its preparations for the New Zealand Test series in Perth. "I am extremely excited about being a part of the team in a more formal and meaningful role in the coming years," Hussey said. "This team has achieved so much in recent times, to which I hope I can add value to the coaching and playing groups ahead of what will be an exciting and challenging period," he added. "Mike has been a highly valued part of our staff in the past and brings a considerable skill set which is complementary to the coaches and players. Not only is his expertise as a player and coach across multiple formats, competitions, and countries invaluable, but so are his qualities as a person," Australia head coach Andrew McDonald said. (ANI)

item.title: "Would rather not destroy rest of the country": Trump's Iran war tone changes after midterm drubbing
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated he would rather not destroy what remains of Iran but may have to, adopting a hesitant tone following the Republicans' midterm defeat. He noted that a final decision on ...
item.content:encoded:
"Would rather not destroy rest of the country": Trump's Iran war tone changes after midterm drubbing US President Donald Trump stated he would rather not destroy what remains of Iran but may have to, adopting a hesitant tone following the Republicans' midterm defeat. He noted that a final decision on the war is approaching soon. ANI | Updated: 06-11-2026 09:49 IST | Created: 06-11-2026 09:49 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump has indicated that he would rather not destroy what remains of Iran but acknowledged that he may have to, adopting a more hesitant line than his previous threats against Tehran following his Republican Party's setback in the US midterm elections. Addressing reporters in the Oval Office on Thursday (local time), Trump noted that a final decision on whether the war was close to escalating was imminent. "I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I'll have to," he stated, adding, "You'll know soon enough." He described the ultimate choice in terms of permanence. "We'll make a decision, do we want to go further and just certify it by certifying it, meaning where it'll never happen again?" Trump remarked, estimating that rebuilding the nation would require a quarter of a century. "I think it'll take them 25 years to rebuild the country." This language contrasts with his earlier posture, during which he warned that American forces had yet to begin "destroying what's left" of Iran, keeping additional energy infrastructure and bridges as targets. Previously, during another phase of the conflict, he maintained that reaching a deal was only possible if the United States blew up the remainder of the nation and its leadership. These remarks follow a specific pledge delivered on October 8, when Trump stated that talks with Iran were productive and explicitly ruled out military action before the national ballot. "We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd," he noted at the time, while American media outlets reported that indirect negotiations were ongoing. That commitment has since expired following the conclusion of the vote. Earlier reports had already suggested his hesitation to completely eliminate Iran's remaining military capacity due to the extensive duration required for national reconstruction. Domestically, the ongoing war has created political friction for the administration, keeping fuel costs elevated and contributing to a decline in public approval ratings as the election approached. Whether the administration pursues further military strikes or a negotiated settlement will ultimately dictate the trajectory of a conflict that has severely disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and deeply unsettled energy markets. (ANI)

item.title: "No negotiations till US fulfils seven conditions": Iran security chief says Russia condemned US-Israel strikes
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has condemned the US and Israeli strikes against Iran and its nuclear facilities, Iran's security chief, Major General Mohsen Rezaei, said as Russia offered support to ...
item.content:encoded:
"No negotiations till US fulfils seven conditions": Iran security chief says Russia condemned US-Israel strikes Russian President Vladimir Putin has condemned the US and Israeli strikes against Iran and its nuclear facilities, Iran's security chief, Major General Mohsen Rezaei, said as Russia offered support to end the ongoing war in West Asia, as per IRNA. ANI | Updated: 06-11-2026 09:48 IST | Created: 06-11-2026 09:48 IST

Russian President Vladimir Putin meets Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei in Moscow (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Russia

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Russian President Vladimir Putin has condemned the US and Israeli strikes against Iran and its nuclear facilities, Iran's security chief, Major General Mohsen Rezaei, said as Russia offered support to end the ongoing war in West Asia, as per IRNA. Rezaei met Putin at the Kremlin Palace on Thursday and delivered a message from Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Khamenei. Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Rezaei said that there will be no negotiations with the United States regarding the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, untill Iran's seven conditions are met. Rezaei said, "Russian President Vladimir Putin had forcefully condemned the US and Israel's military aggression against Iran, including the strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities." "Until the Americans fulfil our seven conditions, neither will the Strait of Hormuz be opened, nor will there be any negotiations," he added. Iranian broadcaster Press TV also reported, citing a source, that Rezaei had stated that Tehran does not consider the diplomatic process to be worthwhile until all of the seven conditions are simultaneously implemented. During the meeting, the Russian President stated that Moscow is ready to make every possible effort to bring the ongoing US-Iran war to an end. "Mr Putin said he will do everything he can to help bring the war to an end," Rezaei said, according to Press TV. The two sides also discussed energy cooperation, particularly the construction of gas pipelines connecting Russia and Iran. "We discussed the construction of gas pipelines from Russia to Iran, which would allow Iran to address its domestic gas shortages while also selling Russian gas to neighbouring countries," Rezaei said. The meeting between Putin and Rezaei came amid the United States weighing in on resuming military strikes against Iran after Democrats swept the US Midterm elections. Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held telephone conversations with his counterparts from Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Oman amid diplomatic efforts in the region. (ANI)
